The estate can collect damages from the driver. A post-crash refusal of a transfusion on sincere religious grounds is judged under the duty to mitigate damages, and contributory negligence—a complete bar only for fault that helps cause the original harm—does not erase the claim. Where that refusal counts as reasonable, the estate recovers for the death; where mitigation is judged by a purely objective standard, the estate recovers only the damages that would have remained after the transfusion the physician said would have produced a full recovery.
CONFIDENCE: 82
